name: Point Lowly Lighthouse
reason: SATC page: 1883 lighthouse, free, open, at the cuttlefish area; a landmark a visitor can walk up to and see.

name: Whyalla Jetty
reason: SATC page: the only circular jetty in the Southern Hemisphere, 315 m, free, for walking and sightseeing; Wikivoyage also lists it.

name: Whyalla Foreshore
reason: SATC page: foreshore and marina on Spencer Gulf with swimming beach, dolphin viewing and Hummock Hill Lookout; distinct from the jetty as a beach/marina stop.

name: Jim Pollock Whyalla Wetlands
reason: SATC page describes a picnic/recreation area with BBQs, playground and stormwater lakes on a former aerodrome: an ordinary local park.

name: Elvis Presley Museum Whyalla
reason: For: SATC lists a 50-year private Elvis collection filling a home, a quirky stop, free. Against: a private home visited by phone booking with the owner, one source, may not be there on arrival.

name: Mount Laura Homestead Museum
reason: SATC page: National Trust museum in the 1914-era homestead and Gay Street cottage, from $5, open most weekdays.

name: Wittelbee Conservation Park
reason: SATC and parks.sa.gov.au name the headland with bushwalking tracks, seabird foreshore and samphire flats; free. Needs a real pin near Wittelbee Point (Decres Bay Road, Ceduna area), not the -37.17,139.86 candidate coordinates.

name: Point Bell Conservation Park
reason: SATC/parks.sa: rocky point with granite boulders, long beaches and dunes for swimming, fishing and camping; 4WD access only. Second-tier coastal stop a guide names.

name: Calpatanna Waterhole Conservation Park
reason: Single SATC page; a roadside park on the highway with no named walk, lookout or feature beyond a waterhole; generic bushwalking and camping. Searched SATC only.

name: Corrobinnie Hill Conservation Park
reason: SATC page: large granite outcrop with views to the Gawler Ranges, a popular picnic and boulder-climbing stop, free (4WD only).

name: Mount Hill Lookout
reason: No counted source names a Mount Hill lookout; southaustralia.com lists Cleve Hills Lookout and Observation Hill instead (the latter judged separately).

name: Yandinga Falls
reason: parks.sa.gov.au Gawler Ranges NP names Yandinga Falls and the Yandinga Five Falls walk as a park highlight.

name: Kolay Mirica Falls
reason: parks.sa.gov.au Gawler Ranges NP names Kolay Mirica Falls and a Mirica Falls walk among the park's spectacular sites.

name: Paney Homestead
reason: parks.sa.gov.au Gawler Ranges NP names Paney Homestead and the Old Paney Heritage trail as station-history sites to visit.

name: Ucontitchie Hill
reason: SATC page: domed granite inselberg of international geological significance with wave structures at its base; free, climbable.

name: Wudinna Granite Trail
reason: Wikivoyage Wudinna Do: 9 km walk/bike trail to Little Mount Wudinna through Polda Rock reserve, with wildlife.

name: Whites Knob Edward John Eyre Sculptures
reason: Only Wikivoyage Eyre Peninsula/Kimba lists it ('explorer statues on a scenic hill', dead link, 2015); a short statue stop with no confirmation it is current.

name: Workshop 26 Kimba Creative Quarter
reason: SATC page: a women's collective of small shipping-container shops with a barista coffee; essentially shops and a cafe, part-week hours.

name: Kimba Gawler Ranges Historical Society
reason: SATC page: Kimba Museum with 1908 Pioneer House, one-teacher school, pioneer store and tractor collection, from $5 (Wed-Fri).

name: Iron Knob Visitor Centre and Museum
reason: Wikivoyage Iron Knob See and the town's own and whyalla.com pages: free mining museum with equipment, minerals, photos and theatrette, weekdays.

name: Iron Knob Mine Tours
reason: A tour/operator rather than a place: volunteer minibus tours leave from the Iron Knob visitor centre to the pit viewpoint; mention in the Iron Knob museum bio instead (duplicate of Iron Knob Visitor Centre and Museum).

name: Middleback Range
reason: No counted source names it as a place to go (searched SATC, Wikivoyage); working iron-ore hills.

name: Corunna Station
reason: No counted source; a working pastoral station without public visitor access.

name: Lake Greenly
reason: No counted source names it; salt lake with nothing for visitors to do.

name: Observation Hill Lookout
reason: SATC page: Cleve bushland hill (Ticklebelly Hill) with walking trail and lookout over the town; southaustralia.com also lists it.

name: Federation Hill Lookout
reason: SATC and Cleve council: 360-degree views from the Darke Peak Ranges via an easy 260 m walk from the car park, free.

name: Cummins Mosaic Trail
reason: SATC and Explore Cummins: free self-guided trail of mosaic artworks through town, a half-hour-plus walk.

name: Gulf and Ranges Trail
reason: SATC page: 4 km hiking/cycling loop at Crag Point with geology signage and Spencer Gulf and ranges views; free.

name: Freycinet Trail
reason: SATC page: 12 km coastal hiking/cycling/driving trail along Fitzgerald Bay to Point Lowly with a 4 km walking section; free.

name: Saltmarsh Trail Eight Mile Creek
reason: SATC: two short QR-guided mangrove/saltmarsh walks, minor local nature trails with one source and no draw beyond them.

name: Eyre Peninsula Railway
reason: For: SATC lists the Port Lincoln Railway Museum in the heritage station, from $6. Against: open Wednesday afternoons only (about 3 h a week), one source, not there whenever a visitor arrives; the name 'Eyre Peninsula Railway' is a line, not a place.

name: Nautilus Arts Centre
reason: For: SATC lists a 100-year-old foreshore building with two free galleries and a theatre. Against: mainly a performance venue and community arts centre, one source, galleries weekday hours.
